## Overview
The Clinic Management System is an enterprise software solution designed for medium-sized hospitals and clinics to manage patient admissions, electronic medical records, scheduling, and billing. It ensures high availability, strict regulatory compliance, and rapid clinical workflows across hybrid cloud and on-premise environments.

## Key Elements
- **People:** Patient, Clinician / Doctor, Receptionist / Admin, Billing Specialist, Compliance / IT Auditor, Hospital Executive
- **Software Systems:** Clinic Management System, External Lab & Imaging Systems, Payment Gateway & Insurance Clearinghouse, Identity Provider (IdP), Business Analytics / Reporting Service
- **Containers/Infrastructure:** On-Premise Kubernetes Cluster, AWS Region (`eu-central-1`), Local Survivability Caching Nodes

## Relationships
- **Patient, Clinician, Receptionist, Billing Specialist, Hospital Executive** interact with **Clinic Management System** via HTTPS / TLS 1.3
- **Clinic Management System** integrates with **External Lab & Imaging Systems** via HL7 FHIR REST APIs
- **Clinic Management System** communicates with **Payment Gateway & Insurance Clearinghouse** via secure REST/SOAP APIs
- **Clinic Management System** authenticates users against **Identity Provider** using OAuth 2.0 / OIDC with Multi-Factor Authentication
- **Clinic Management System** publishes sanitized telemetry and metrics to **Business Analytics / Reporting Service** via Kafka / Debezium message streams

## Technology Stack
- **Kubernetes (`on-prem-k8s` & AWS `eu-central-1`):** Hybrid cloud container orchestration ensuring local survivability during network partitions
- **HL7 FHIR & REST/SOAP:** Interoperability standards for lab, imaging, and external billing integrations
- **OAuth 2.0 / OIDC:** Secure enterprise authentication and multi-factor access control
- **AES-256 & TLS 1.3:** Encryption standards mandated for data at rest and in transit to satisfy HIPAA and GDPR
- **Kafka / Debezium:** Asynchronous event streaming for decoupled analytics ETL pipelines

## Rationale
This architecture uses a hybrid deployment model with local survivability caching to guarantee 99.99% uptime and clinical continuity during internet outages. Decoupling the reporting pipeline via event streaming protects core database performance, ensuring EMR screen loads remain below the required 1-second P95 threshold.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
The Clinic Management System is a hybrid cloud platform designed for medium-sized hospitals to handle patient admissions, scheduling, electronic medical records (EMR), and billing securely. It guarantees high availability (99.99%), strict regulatory compliance (HIPAA/GDPR), and 10-year data retention.

## Key Elements
- **Users**: Patient, Clinician/Doctor, Receptionist/Admin, Billing Specialist, Compliance/IT Auditor, Hospital Executive.
- **Frontend Container**: Single Page Application (TypeScript / React).
- **Edge Container**: API Gateway (Kong / Envoy) with mTLS.
- **Backend Containers**: Clinical Service (Go), Scheduling Service (Node.js), Billing Service (Java / Spring Boot), Audit & Compliance Log Service (Go), Integration Service / FHIR Facade (Go).
- **Infrastructure Containers**: Event Bus (Apache Kafka / RabbitMQ), Databases (PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Redis), Object Storage (encrypted S3-compatible).
- **External Systems**: External Lab & Imaging Systems, Payment Gateway & Insurance Clearinghouse, Identity Provider (IdP), Business Analytics / Reporting Service.

## Relationships
- **SPA to API Gateway**: HTTPS / JSON.
- **API Gateway to Backend Services**: Internal gRPC and REST over mTLS.
- **Backend Services to Event Bus**: Asynchronous domain event publishing (Kafka/RabbitMQ).
- **Integration Service to External Systems**: HL7 FHIR APIs for lab and imaging interoperability.
- **Backend Services to Data Stores**: TLS-encrypted connections to PostgreSQL, MongoDB, and Redis.

## Technology Stack
- **Frontend**: TypeScript, React, Nginx/CDN for rapid client-side rendering.
- **Gateway & Routing**: Kong / Envoy for rate limiting, mTLS, and circuit breaking.
- **Backend Languages**: Go (high-performance clinical and audit services), Node.js (scheduling), Java / Spring Boot (robust transactional billing).
- **Databases**: PostgreSQL (transactional clinical/scheduling data), MongoDB (immutable audit logs), Redis (caching).
- **Messaging & Infrastructure**: Apache Kafka / RabbitMQ for event-driven decoupling; Kubernetes (on-prem-k8s and AWS eu-central-1) managed via ArgoCD.

## Rationale
Isolating clinical, scheduling, and billing microservices via an Event Bus ensures that third-party payment or lab outages never block critical patient care workflows. Polyglot persistence, automated tiered archiving to encrypted S3 storage, and strict hybrid Kubernetes deployment patterns collectively satisfy the 99.99% availability, sub-second EMR performance, and 10-year retention mandates.

## Overview
The Clinic Management System is a hybrid cloud platform designed to manage patient admissions, electronic medical records (EMR), scheduling, and billing for medium-sized hospitals and clinics. It ensures strict HIPAA/GDPR compliance, 99.99% availability, and long-term data retention.

## Key Elements
- **Frontend Container**: TypeScript, React, Nginx/CDN single-page application.
- **Internal Components**: Authentication & Session Manager, Role-Based Router & Shell, Clinical EMR View Component, API Client Layer, Local Persistence Manager (IndexedDB), Cryptographic Vault Manager.
- **Edge Container**: Kong / Envoy.
- **Backend Services**: Clinical Service (Go), Scheduling Service (Node.js), Billing Service (Java / Spring Boot), Audit & Compliance Log Service (Go), Integration Service / FHIR Facade (Go).
- **Data & Infrastructure**: Apache Kafka / RabbitMQ, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Redis, Encrypted S3-compatible Object Storage.
- **Personas**: Patient, Clinician / Doctor, Receptionist / Admin, Billing Specialist, Compliance / IT Auditor, Hospital Executive.

## Relationships
- **Patient, Clinician, Receptionist, Billing Specialist, Auditor, Executive** -> **Frontend Container**: Accesses role-based portals and workflows [HTTPS / JSON]
- **Frontend Container** -> **Edge Container**: Sends API requests [HTTPS / JSON over TLS 1.3]
- **Clinical EMR View Component** -> **Local Persistence Manager**: Reads/Writes encrypted drafts [IndexedDB / Web Crypto API]
- **Integration Service** -> **External Lab & Imaging Systems**: Interoperability data exchange [HL7 FHIR APIs]

## Technology Stack
- **Frontend**: TypeScript, React, Nginx, Global CDN for optimized client-side rendering and static asset delivery.
- **Security**: Web Crypto API for client-side encryption, OIDC/OAuth2 via Identity Provider for multi-factor authentication.
- **Backend**: Go, Node.js, and Java Spring Boot microservices chosen for domain-specific performance and reliability.
- **Databases & Messaging**: PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Redis, Apache Kafka / RabbitMQ supporting active-active resilience.
- **Deployment**: Kubernetes (`on-prem-k8s` and AWS `eu-central-1`) with non-root Nginx container hardening.

## Rationale
This hybrid architecture combines on-premises Kubernetes clusters with cloud infrastructure to satisfy strict data residency regulations and 99.99% availability requirements. Encrypted client-side storage and role-based access control ensure full HIPAA and GDPR compliance while maintaining sub-second EMR performance.

Edge Container.analysis:
## Overview
The Clinic Management System is a hybrid cloud platform designed to manage patient admissions, electronic medical records (EMR), scheduling, and billing for medium-sized hospitals and clinics. It ensures high availability, strict compliance, and rapid clinical workflows.

## Key Elements
- Patients, Clinicians, Receptionists, Billing Specialists, Auditors, and Executives
- Frontend Container (React, TypeScript, Nginx/CDN)
- Edge Container (Kong / Envoy API Gateway with Authentication, Rate Limiting, and Telemetry plugins)
- Clinical Service, Scheduling Service, Billing Service, Audit Log Service, and Integration Service (Go, Node.js, Java Spring Boot)
- Apache Kafka / RabbitMQ Event Bus
- PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Redis, and Encrypted S3-compatible Object Storage
- External Identity Provider (IdP), Payment Gateway, and Lab/Imaging Systems

## Relationships
- Frontend Container -> Edge Container: API requests [HTTPS / JSON]
- Edge Container -> Internal Services: Internal routing [gRPC and REST over mTLS]
- Edge Container -> Identity Provider: User authentication [OAuth 2.0 / OIDC with MFA]
- Integration Service -> Lab & Imaging Systems: Interoperability [HL7 FHIR APIs]

## Technology Stack
- Kong / Envoy: API gateway and edge routing for high performance and security
- Redis: Tenant-aware rate limiting and token validation cache with L2 fallback
- Go, Java Spring Boot, Node.js: Microservices backend implementation
- Kubernetes (on-prem-k8s) & AWS (eu-central-1): Hybrid cloud infrastructure
- Prometheus: Telemetry and observability metrics monitoring

## Rationale
This architecture uses a hybrid cloud deployment with active-active edge routing to meet stringent 99.99% availability and 1-second EMR load time requirements. Centralized mTLS routing and robust encryption satisfy HIPAA and GDPR compliance mandates.

Clinical Service.analysis:
## Overview
The Clinic Management System is a hybrid cloud platform designed to manage patient admissions, electronic medical records (EMR), scheduling, and billing for medium-sized healthcare facilities. It ensures high availability, strict HIPAA/GDPR compliance, and sub-second performance for critical clinical workflows.

## Key Elements
*   **Users**: Patient, Clinician / Doctor, Receptionist / Admin, Billing Specialist, Compliance / IT Auditor, Hospital Executive.
*   **External Systems**: External Lab & Imaging Systems, Payment Gateway & Insurance Clearinghouse, Identity Provider (IdP), Business Analytics / Reporting Service.
*   **Containers**: Frontend Container (React, TypeScript), Edge Container (Kong / Envoy), Clinical Service (Go), Scheduling Service (Node.js), Billing Service (Spring Boot), Audit & Compliance Log Service (Go), Integration Service / FHIR Facade (Go).
*   **Clinical Service Components**: EMR Management Component, Patient Admission & Demographics Component, Clinical Data Access Repository, Audit & Event Publisher Component.
*   **Data & Infrastructure**: Apache Kafka / RabbitMQ, PostgreSQL, Redis, Encrypted S3-compatible Object Storage, Kubernetes (on-prem-k8s, AWS eu-central-1).

## Relationships
*   Edge Container -> Clinical Service: Routes incoming requests via internal mTLS [gRPC, REST over mTLS]
*   Clinical Service -> Clinical Data Access Repository: Reads and writes clinical records and cache [TLS-encrypted PostgreSQL, Redis]
*   Clinical Data Access Repository -> Object Storage: Archives long-term medical records [Encrypted S3-compatible APIs]
*   Clinical Service -> Event Bus: Publishes asynchronous domain events [Apache Kafka / RabbitMQ]
*   Integration Service -> External Systems: Exchanges health data [HL7 FHIR APIs]

## Technology Stack
*   **Go**: Powers the Clinical Service, Audit Service, and FHIR Facade for high performance and low latency.
*   **React & TypeScript**: Used for the responsive frontend container.
*   **PostgreSQL & Redis**: Provides ACID-compliant relational storage and high-speed in-memory caching for sub-second EMR retrieval.
*   **Apache Kafka / RabbitMQ**: Handles asynchronous event-driven messaging to decouple microservices.
*   **Kubernetes**: Orchestrates hybrid multi-region deployments with Horizontal Pod Autoscalers (HPA).
*   **OpenTelemetry**: Captures distributed traces and structured logs for system observability.

## Rationale
The microservices architecture combined with active-active Kubernetes deployments guarantees 99.99% availability and high resilience. Utilizing Go for core clinical components ensures sub-second P95 performance while maintaining robust AES-256 encryption and comprehensive audit trails for HIPAA and GDPR compliance.

Scheduling Service.analysis:
## Overview
- The system is a Clinic Management System designed for medium-sized hospitals and clinics to handle patient records, scheduling, and billing securely.
- The core purpose of the Scheduling Service container is to manage patient and resource bookings with real-time conflict prevention while ensuring high availability.

## Key Elements
- Patients and Receptionists / Admins (Users)
- Edge Container (Kong / Envoy)
- Scheduling Service (Node.js Container)
- API Router Component (Express.js / Fastify)
- Booking Engine Component (Node.js)
- Availability Cache Component (Redis Cluster)
- Notification Dispatcher Component
- Databases (PostgreSQL)
- Event Bus (Apache Kafka)

## Relationships
- Edge Container -> API Router Component: Routes requests via mTLS [gRPC and REST over mTLS]
- API Router Component -> Booking Engine Component: Delegates requests [In-process TypeScript interfaces]
- Booking Engine Component -> Availability Cache Component: Acquires distributed locks and checks availability [TCP with TLS, `rediss://`]
- Booking Engine Component -> Databases: Persists booking data [TLS-encrypted PostgreSQL connections]
- Notification Dispatcher Component -> Event Bus: Publishes domain events [Apache Kafka using `kafkajs` over TLS]

## Technology Stack
- Node.js & TypeScript: Chosen for rapid iteration on complex scheduling logic and calendar calculations.
- Redis Cluster: Implements Redlock for distributed locking to prevent resource clashes and double-bookings.
- PostgreSQL: Provides ACID-compliant relational data storage for appointment records.
- Apache Kafka: Handles asynchronous event publishing for notifications and analytics.
- Kubernetes (Hybrid): Ensures active-active high availability (99.99%) across on-prem-k8s and eu-central-1.

## Rationale
- This architecture isolates calendar logic and leverages Redis Redlock to prevent race conditions during peak concurrency, fulfilling stringent uptime and performance requirements.
- Hybrid cloud deployment and robust event-driven components ensure HIPAA compliance, high availability, and seamless interoperability.

## Overview
The Clinic Management System is a hybrid cloud platform managing patient admissions, EMRs, scheduling, and billing for healthcare facilities. It ensures HIPAA/GDPR compliance, high availability, and secure interoperability.

## Key Elements
- Billing Service (Java / Spring Boot container)
- Claim Management Component (Drools rules engine)
- Payment Processing Component (Resilience4j circuit breakers)
- Billing API & Dashboard Component (Dual-datasource routing)
- Security & Authorization Interceptor (JWT/OAuth2 validation)
- PostgreSQL Database (Primary Write-Master and Read-Replica)

- Apache Kafka: Delivers reliable asynchronous messaging backed by Transactional Outbox pattern
- Resilience4j: Implements circuit breaking to prevent cascading failures during clearinghouse outages
- Drools: Powers the automated claim validation rules engine

## Rationale
This architecture ensures 99.99% availability and stringent HIPAA/GDPR compliance through component isolation, read-replica query offloading, and robust transactional safeguards. The chosen Java Spring Boot stack and resilient integration patterns guarantee data integrity and operational continuity for critical healthcare financial workflows.

Audit & Compliance Log Service.analysis:
## Overview
[The Audit & Compliance Log Service is a backend microservice in Go designed to manage immutable regulatory audit trails, compliance reporting, and real-time anomaly alerting for the Clinic Management System. It ensures strict HIPAA and GDPR compliance with a mandatory 10-year data retention policy and 99.99% availability.]

## Key Elements
* Audit & Compliance Log Service (Go container)
* Event Ingestion Engine (Go component)
* Compliance API Handler (Go component)
* Retention & Archival Worker (Go component)
* Anomaly Detection & Alerting Engine (Go component)
* Event Bus (Apache Kafka / RabbitMQ)
* Databases (MongoDB)
* Object Storage (Encrypted S3-compatible with WORM Compliance Mode)
* Edge Container (Kong / Envoy)

## Relationships
* Edge Container -> Compliance API Handler: Routes requests via internal mTLS [gRPC and REST over mTLS]
* Event Bus -> Event Ingestion Engine: Consumes security and access events [Apache Kafka]
* Event Ingestion Engine -> MongoDB: Stores audit logs [TLS-encrypted connections]
* Event Ingestion Engine -> Anomaly Detection & Alerting Engine: Forwards streaming events [Internal Go Channel]
* Retention & Archival Worker -> Object Storage: Archives historical logs [TLS with WORM Compliance Mode]
* Anomaly Detection & Alerting Engine -> Edge Container: Dispatches webhooks/alerts [HTTPS over TLS]

## Technology Stack
* Go: Chosen for high-throughput, non-blocking concurrency via Go routines and low memory footprint.
* Apache Kafka / RabbitMQ: Provides reliable event streaming, dead-letter queues (DLQ), and backpressure handling.
* MongoDB: Stores active audit logs securely with AES-256 encryption at rest.
* Encrypted S3-compatible Object Storage: Enforces AWS Object Lock in Compliance Mode for tamper-proof 10-year data retention.
* OpenTelemetry & Prometheus: Monitors ingestion lag, processing latency, and archival job success rates.

## Rationale
[Decomposing the service into dedicated ingestion, archival, API, and alerting components isolates heavy workloads and protects ingestion throughput. This architecture satisfies rigorous healthcare security mandates, high availability, and 10-year regulatory retention without performance degradation.]

## Overview
The Clinic Management System manages patient admissions, electronic medical records, scheduling, and billing for medium-sized hospitals and clinics. It ensures high availability, strict HIPAA/GDPR compliance, and interoperability across hybrid cloud environments.

- Resource Mapper & Validator (`go-fhir` models)

- Envoy sidecar & Kubernetes clusters (`on-prem-k8s`, `eu-central-1`)

- Go (with `Gin`/`Fiber`, `go-fhir`, and `sarama`/`segmentio/kafka-go`): Chosen for high performance, sub-second ingestion, and robust concurrency.

- Kubernetes & Envoy: Deployed across `on-prem-k8s` and `eu-central-1` to guarantee 99.99% active-active uptime and mTLS security.
- Encrypted S3-compatible Object Storage: Secures DLQ payloads with immutable object locking to meet 10-year audit retention mandates.
- SMART-on-FHIR OAuth2: Secures clinician and patient-access scopes for interoperability.

## Rationale
This architecture ensures robust interoperability through standardized HL7 FHIR APIs while meeting stringent HIPAA/GDPR security and 99.99% availability requirements. The hybrid cloud design, event-driven DLQ pattern, and Go-based facade provide scalable, fault-tolerant clinical data exchange.

Event Bus.analysis:
## Overview
The Clinic Management System manages patient admissions, EMRs, scheduling, and billing for healthcare facilities. It utilizes a hybrid cloud architecture to ensure high availability, stringent security, and compliance with healthcare regulations.

## Key Elements
- **Users**: Patient, Clinician / Doctor, Receptionist / Admin, Billing Specialist, Compliance / IT Auditor, Hospital Executive.
- **External Systems**: External Lab & Imaging Systems, Payment Gateway & Insurance Clearinghouse, Identity Provider (IdP), Business Analytics / Reporting Service.
- **Containers**: Frontend Container, Edge Container, Clinical Service, Scheduling Service, Billing Service, Audit & Compliance Log Service, Integration Service / FHIR Facade, Event Bus, Databases, Object Storage.
- **Event Bus Components**: Kafka Broker Cluster (KRaft Mode), Schema Registry (Avro), Kafka Connect (Debezium), DLQ & Retry Router, Event Governance & Access Control Layer (Apache Ranger / mTLS).

## Relationships
- **Frontend Container -> Edge Container**: Routes client traffic [HTTPS / gRPC].
- **Edge Container -> Microservices (Clinical, Scheduling, Billing)**: Reverse proxies authenticated requests [HTTP/2].
- **Microservices -> Event Bus (Kafka Broker Cluster)**: Publishes and consumes domain events [TCP / Kafka Wire Protocol].
- **Microservices -> Schema Registry**: Validates event schemas [HTTP/REST].
- **Microservices -> Event Governance**: Authenticates and authorizes operations [mTLS / SASL/SCRAM].
- **Kafka Broker Cluster -> DLQ & Retry Router**: Forwards unprocessable events [Kafka Wire Protocol].

## Technology Stack
- **Frontend**: TypeScript, React, Nginx/CDN for rapid responsive EMR UI (<1s P95).
- **Edge**: Kong / Envoy for API gateway routing and security enforcement.
- **Microservices**: Go (Clinical, Integration, Audit), Node.js (Scheduling), Java / Spring Boot (Billing) for optimal performance and concurrency.
- **Event Bus**: Apache Kafka (KRaft mode) with Confluent Schema Registry (Avro) and Debezium for reliable asynchronous messaging and CDC.
- **Storage**: PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Redis, and Encrypted S3-compatible Object Storage for ACID compliance and 10-year retention.

## Rationale
This architecture uses an event-driven microservices pattern with Apache Kafka to guarantee 99.99% active-active availability by decoupling critical clinical and billing workflows. Strict security controls, encrypted tiered storage, and hybrid-cloud replication satisfy HIPAA/GDPR mandates and 10-year data retention requirements without sacrificing EMR performance.

Databases.analysis:
## Overview
The Clinic Management System is a hybrid cloud platform designed to manage patient admissions, electronic medical records, scheduling, and billing for healthcare facilities. It ensures high availability, strict HIPAA/GDPR compliance, and seamless interoperability.

## Key Elements
- Users: Patient, Clinician / Doctor, Receptionist / Admin, Billing Specialist, Compliance / IT Auditor, Hospital Executive
- External Systems: External Lab & Imaging Systems, Payment Gateway & Insurance Clearinghouse, Identity Provider (IdP), Business Analytics / Reporting Service
- Containers: Frontend Container (TypeScript, React, Nginx/CDN), Edge Container (Kong / Envoy), Clinical Service (Go), Scheduling Service (Node.js), Billing Service (Java / Spring Boot), Audit & Compliance Log Service (Go), Integration Service / FHIR Facade (Go), Event Bus (Apache Kafka / RabbitMQ), Databases (PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Redis), Object Storage (Encrypted S3-compatible)
- Database Sub-components: Primary OLTP Store (PostgreSQL with Patroni), Document Store (MongoDB), In-Memory Cache (Redis), Connection Pooler (PgBouncer)

## Relationships
- Clinical Service -> Databases: Reads and writes clinical data and cache via TLS-encrypted connections (PostgreSQL, Redis)
- Scheduling Service -> Databases: Reads and writes scheduling data and cache via TLS-encrypted connections (PostgreSQL, Redis)
- Billing Service -> Databases: Reads and writes billing data via TLS-encrypted connections (PostgreSQL)
- Audit & Compliance Log Service -> Databases: Stores immutable audit logs via TLS-encrypted connections (MongoDB)
- Databases -> Object Storage: Pipes automated, daily snapshots for 10-year retention

## Technology Stack
- PostgreSQL: Active-Passive hot standby cluster managed by Patroni for ACID compliance in billing and scheduling
- MongoDB: Replica set with immutable collections for EMR and audit trails
- Redis: Clustered in-memory cache with AOF/RDB persistence for sub-second EMR screen loads
- PgBouncer: Connection pooling for resource management and availability
- KMS: Centralized Key Management Service for AES-256 data-at-rest encryption and column-level tokenization

## Rationale
This architecture guarantees 99.99% availability and robust data integrity through proven active-passive replication and multi-database polyglot persistence. It satisfies strict HIPAA and GDPR regulations via AES-256 encryption, TLS 1.3 in transit, and tokenization capabilities.

Object Storage.analysis:
## Overview
The Clinic Management System provides patient registration, EMR, scheduling, and billing for healthcare facilities with high availability. It uses a hybrid architecture spanning on-premise Kubernetes and AWS (`eu-central-1`) to meet strict HIPAA and GDPR mandates.

## Key Elements
- **Users**: Patient, Clinician / Doctor, Receptionist / Admin, Billing Specialist, Compliance / IT Auditor, Hospital Executive
- **External Systems**: External Lab & Imaging Systems, Payment Gateway & Insurance Clearinghouse, Identity Provider (IdP), Business Analytics / Reporting Service
- **Containers**: Frontend (React, TypeScript), Edge (Kong / Envoy), Clinical Service (Go), Scheduling (Node.js), Billing (Java/Spring Boot), Audit Service (Go), Integration Service (Go), Kafka/RabbitMQ, Databases (PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Redis), Object Storage (MinIO / Ceph)
- **Object Storage Components**: Storage Gateway, Encryption & Key Management (Vault/AWS KMS), Lifecycle & Tiering Engine, Audit & Compliance Guardrail

## Relationships
- **Clinical Service -> Storage Gateway**: Uploads/retrieves EMR assets via HTTPS / S3 API
- **Storage Gateway -> Audit & Compliance Guardrail**: Validates immutability policies via Internal gRPC
- **Storage Gateway -> Encryption Component**: Applies AES-256 via Internal gRPC
- **Storage Gateway -> MinIO / Ceph Cluster**: Persists objects across hybrid nodes via S3 API

## Technology Stack
- **MinIO / Ceph**: Cloud-agnostic S3-compatible backend ensuring identical hybrid behavior
- **AES-256 & WORM**: Mandatory encryption and Write-Once-Read-Many object locking for compliance
- **Prometheus & PagerDuty**: Metrics, tracing, and alerting for 99.99% availability SLAs
- **Go & Java**: High-performance backend runtime stack

## Rationale
This hybrid architecture uses cloud-agnostic S3 storage with automated tiering and WORM locking to satisfy strict 10-year retention and compliance mandates. Component-level separation guarantees sub-second active record retrieval and robust disaster recovery across on-premise and cloud environments.
